428	// collectFactArtifacts reads facts/<slug>/facts.ndjson, recovering each stream's
429	// logical branch (resolveFactStreamBranch), and registers a FactsRef on art.
430	// Streams are keyed by branch and emitted in branch order.
431	func collectFactArtifacts(art *brainwire.BrainArtifact, brainDir string) ([]publishArtifact, error) {
432		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
433		if err != nil {
434			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load facts privacy manifest: %w", err)
435		}
436		guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
437		if err != nil {
438			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load facts privacy policy: %w", err)
439		}
440		entries, _, err := brainstore.ReadPrivacyDirectory(brainDir, factstore.DirName, "publish facts")
441		if err != nil {
442			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
443				return nil, nil
444			}
445			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts: %w", err)
446		}
447	
448		dirs := subdirNames(entries)
449		sort.Strings(dirs)
450	
451		type factStream struct {
452			branch string
453			data   []byte
454		}
455		var streams []factStream
456		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
457		for _, dir := range dirs {
458			data, ok, err := readBrainBlob(brainDir, filepath.Join(factstore.DirName, dir, factstore.FileName))
459			if err != nil {
460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", dir, err)
461			}
462			if !ok {
463				continue
464			}
465			branch, err := resolveFactStreamBranch(dir, data)
466			if err != nil {
467				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", dir, err)
468			}
469			if branch == "" {
470				continue
471			}
472			if _, dup := seen[branch]; dup {
473				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: duplicate branch stream %q", dir, branch)
474			}
475			seen[branch] = struct{}{}
476			streams = append(streams, factStream{branch: branch, data: data})
477		}
478		sort.Slice(streams, func(i, j int) bool { return streams[i].branch < streams[j].branch })
479	
480		var out []publishArtifact
481		for _, stream := range streams {
482			// REDACT before the bytes become an artifact. The digest and the manifest
483			// ContentRef must describe what actually leaves, so the redaction has to
484			// happen ahead of both.
485			data, err := redactFactsForEgress(stream.data, guard)
486			if err != nil {
487				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", stream.branch, err)
488			}
489			rel := factstore.FileRelPath(stream.branch)
490			digest := contentDigest(data)
491			art.AddFacts(brainwire.FactsRef{
492				Branch:  stream.branch,
493				Content: brainwire.ContentRef{Digest: digest, Size: int64(len(data)), MediaType: mediaTypeNDJSON, Path: rel},
494			})
495			out = append(out, publishArtifact{Kind: brainKindFacts, Ref: stream.branch, Digest: digest, Data: data})
496		}
497		return out, nil
498	}

500	// redactFactsForEgress re-renders a facts stream with the LOCAL-ONLY provenance
501	// coordinates stripped, which is what `facts sync` has always done and what publish
502	// did not.
503	//
504	// A distilled fact's anchor mixes two kinds of value (see factsync.SanitizeForEgress):
505	// opaque cross-member ids another member can carry but never resolve (session id,
506	// commit, checkpoint, turn), and the coordinates of a private file on THIS machine —
507	// Transcript, a brain-relative transcript path, and Line, a turn offset into it. The
508	// path is not an opaque handle: it is rendered as
509	//
510	//	sessions/main/20260530T174906Z_codex_<session-uuid>_<checkpoint>.jsonl
511	//
512	// so shipping it hands the other side a dated inventory of the member's private
513	// sessions — when each ran, which agent tool ran it — and, with Line, the exact turn
514	// a statement came from. None of it is needed to consume a fact: the reasoning layer
515	// treats a peer's anchor as opaque and never resolves one (ADR-P1).
516	//
517	// factsync.SanitizeForEgress is the SAME redaction the fact-set sync and the
518	// proposal push apply, deliberately rather than a second copy of the rule: the two
519	// egress paths carry the same records to the same service, so they must agree on
520	// what may leave, and one implementation is how that stays true.
521	//
522	// A stream that will not parse is an ERROR, not a stream to ship unredacted. It is
523	// also not a new class of failure: `facts sync` already refuses the same file, so a
524	// brain that cannot publish here could not sync either.
525	func redactFactsForEgress(data []byte, guard sessionReadGuard) ([]byte, error) {
526		records, err := factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(data))
527		if err != nil {
528			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot redact local-only provenance before upload: %w", err)
529		}
530		// Filter before sanitizing: transcript coordinates are needed to recognize
531		// excluded provenance when an anchor has no session ID.
532		records = guardFactRecords(guard, records)
533		var buf bytes.Buffer
534		if err := factmerge.WriteNDJSON(&buf, factsync.SanitizeForEgress(records)); err != nil {
535			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot redact local-only provenance before upload: %w", err)
536		}
537		return buf.Bytes(), nil
538	}

562	// postBrainArtifacts POSTs the bundle to the hosted brain publish endpoint and
563	// maps the response to a clear error or result. It is the only network call in
564	// the command; it runs only after both opt-in gates have passed.
565	func postBrainArtifacts(ctx context.Context, baseURL, repoID, token string, body publishRequestBody) (publishResult, error) {
566		baseURL, err := apiurl.Validate(baseURL)
567		if err != nil {
568			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
569		}
570		payload, err := json.Marshal(body)
571		if err != nil {
572			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: encode request: %w", err)
573		}
574		// The chokepoint check, not a duplicate of the one in runPublish: this is the
575		// only function that turns a repo id into a network target, and it is reachable
576		// from tests and any future caller that did not come through the command. An id
577		// that is not one bare path segment re-addresses the request — url.PathEscape
578		// cannot prevent that, since "." and ".." are unreserved and survive escaping, so
579		// ".." here yields /api/v1/repos/../brain/artifacts, which normalizes to
580		// /api/v1/brain/artifacts with the caller's bearer token and the whole brain
581		// bundle attached. Refuse before http.NewRequest exists.
582		if err := repoid.Validate(repoID); err != nil {
583			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
584		}
585		// Validated ids equal their own escaped form, so the id is concatenated raw.
586		endpoint := strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/") + publishAPIPathPrefix + repoID + publishAPIPathSuffix
587	
588		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, bytes.NewReader(payload))
589		if err != nil {
590			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: build request: %w", err)
591		}
592		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
593		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
594	
595		resp, err := apiurl.WithoutRedirects(publishHTTPClient()).Do(req)
596		if err != nil {
597			// The wrapped error is a *url.Error, whose own Error() renders the target
598			// through url.URL.Redacted() — any userinfo password is printed as "xxxxx".
599			// Interpolating `endpoint` here as well undid exactly that redaction and
600			// printed the cleartext credential. apiurl.Validate now refuses a base URL
601			// carrying userinfo at all, so this is the second of two guards; the target
602			// is still named, by the half of the message that redacts it.
603			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: request failed: %w", err)
604		}
605		defer resp.Body.Close()
606		respBody, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxPublishResponseBytes))
607	
608		switch resp.StatusCode {
609		case http.StatusOK:
610			var result publishResult
611			if err := json.Unmarshal(respBody, &result); err != nil {
612				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: decode server response: %w", err)
613			}
614			// A 200 whose body acknowledges NOTHING is not a success, and reporting it as
615			// one is the worst outcome on this path: the member is told the brain is
616			// published, stops thinking about it, and the hosted brain holds nothing. The
617			// endpoint answers with the coordinate of every artifact it stored, so an
618			// empty `stored` against a non-empty upload means the bytes did not land —
619			// a half-deployed server, a proxy answering `{}` in front of it, or a
620			// response that never came from the endpoint at all. Refuse, and say which
621			// of the two it is rather than guessing on the member's behalf.
622			if len(body.Artifacts) > 0 && len(result.Stored) == 0 {
623				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server answered HTTP 200 but acknowledged storing 0 of the %d artifact(s) sent%s; the brain was NOT published — check that %s is the hosted Entire API and not a proxy in front of it",
624					len(body.Artifacts), publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token), endpoint)
625			}
626			// Stored coordinates must cover exactly the submitted set, once each.
627			expected := make(map[[2]string]bool, len(body.Artifacts))
628			for _, artifact := range body.Artifacts {
629				expected[[2]string{artifact.Kind, artifact.Ref}] = true
630			}
631			complete := len(result.Stored) == len(body.Artifacts)
632			for _, stored := range result.Stored {
633				key := [2]string{stored.Kind, stored.Ref}
634				if !expected[key] {
635					complete = false
636				}
637				delete(expected, key)
638			}
639			if !complete || len(expected) != 0 {
640				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server did not acknowledge every submitted artifact exactly once%s; check the hosted publish response before retrying", publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token))
641			}
642			return result, nil
643		case http.StatusUnauthorized, http.StatusForbidden:
644			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_auth: authentication or push authorization failed (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
645		case http.StatusUnprocessableEntity:
646			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_rejected: server rejected the brain artifacts (HTTP 422)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
647		case http.StatusServiceUnavailable:
648			// The server uses 503 for more than one reason (no hosted brain on this
649			// deployment, publishing disabled for this jurisdiction, a store that is
650			// temporarily read-only), so its own sentence is the only thing that says
651			// WHICH — dropping the body here left the client guessing on the member's
652			// behalf.
653			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unavailable: hosted brain publishing is not available on the server (HTTP 503)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
654		case http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge:
655			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_too_large: the server rejected the brain bundle as too large (HTTP 413); its request body exceeds the hosted publish size limit%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
656		default:
657			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_failed: unexpected server response (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
658		}
659	}

661	// publishStatusDetail renders the server's own `status` field for the
662	// acknowledged-nothing refusal, as " (status \"...\")", or "" when it said nothing.
663	// It goes through the same terminal-safety cleaning as every other server string
664	// this command prints.
665	func publishStatusDetail(status, token string) string {
666		cleaned := httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody([]byte(status)), token)
667		if cleaned == "" {
668			return ""
669		}
670		return " (status " + strconv.Quote(cleaned) + ")"
671	}

673	// publishServerDetail renders a short human-readable reason from a server error body.
674	//
675	// It delegates to httpx, which is the shared renderer for every hosted-API error body
676	// in this repo. The local version this replaced handled the ONE shape the endpoint
677	// documents — huma's {"title","detail"} — and pasted everything else through as a
678	// raw 200-byte prefix. That is exactly the wrong answer for the two shapes that
679	// actually show up when the endpoint is not the thing answering: a proxy's HTML page
680	// (200 bytes of doctype and markup, with the useful part — its <title> — usually past
681	// the cut) and a body carrying control bytes, printed straight into the member's
682	// terminal. httpx renders both, and still prefers the envelope's own detail when the
683	// endpoint did answer.
684	//
685	// Every message this suffixes already prints the status ("(HTTP 404)"), so a body
686	// that merely echoes the status text would render doubled: "unexpected server
687	// response (HTTP 404): not found". The echo is stripped; a body saying more keeps
688	// the part beyond it.
689	func publishServerDetail(body []byte, statusCode int, token string) string {
690		detail := httpx.StripStatusEcho(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody(body),
691			strconv.Itoa(statusCode)+" "+http.StatusText(statusCode))
692		if detail == "" {
693			return ""
694		}
695		// httpx.Redact strips this request's own bearer token from the rendered line: a
696		// server that echoes the Authorization header back would otherwise put it in the
697		// member's stderr, and from there into a CI log or a pasted bug report.
698		return ": " + httpx.Redact(detail, token)
699	}

701	// contentDigest returns the "sha256:"-prefixed lowercase-hex digest of data, the
702	// exact form the wire contract's ContentRef.Digest and the server's VerifyDigest
703	// expect.
704	func contentDigest(data []byte) string {
705		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
706		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
707	}

716	// readBrainBlob binds a payload to its brain-relative path, rejecting symlinks
717	// in every component and validating the opened regular-file descriptor. Missing
718	// files remain optional; unsafe files fail the bundle instead of being omitted.
719	func readBrainBlob(brainDir, rel string) ([]byte, bool, error) {
720		f, present, err := brainstore.OpenMemoryStateFileExpected(brainDir, rel, "publish artifact", nil)
721		if err != nil || !present {
722			return nil, false, err
723		}
724		defer f.Close()
725		max := clibase.SemanticSnapshotMaxBytes()
726		path := f.Name()
727		if info, err := f.Stat(); err != nil {
728			return nil, false, err
729		} else if info.Size() > max {
730			return nil, false, &readBoundExceededError{Source: path, Max: max}
731		}
732		data, err := clibase.SafeReadAll(f, max, path)
733		if err != nil {
734			return nil, false, err
735		}
736		return data, true, nil
737	}

749	// resolveFactStreamBranch validates a stream and recovers the branch that owns
750	// it. Records from other branches are expected content, not corruption: the
751	// hosted pull rebuilds a branch store from the repo-wide feed
752	// (pullHostedFacts), so after a sync on a feature branch the store also
753	// carries teammates' main facts. The owner is therefore not "the records'
754	// branch" but the branch that re-derives the directory name
755	// (factstore.BranchRelDir is deterministic: slug plus a hash of the full name).
756	// Candidates are every branch the records name, plus the directory's own slug
757	// for a store holding only pulled foreign records. A directory no candidate
758	// re-derives is refused — publishing it under a guessed branch would corrupt
759	// the artifact coordinate. (Residual gap: a store of only foreign records for
760	// a branch whose name sanitizes lossily, e.g. "evis/x"; such a stream fails
761	// publish until the branch distills or records a fact of its own.)
762	func resolveFactStreamBranch(dir string, data []byte) (string, error) {
763		records, err := factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(data))
764		if err != nil {
765			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid fact stream: %w", err)
766		}
767		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
768		var candidates []string
769		for i, record := range records {
770			branch := strings.TrimSpace(record.Branch)
771			if branch == "" {
772				return "", fmt.Errorf("fact record %d has no branch", i+1)
773			}
774			if _, dup := seen[branch]; !dup {
775				seen[branch] = struct{}{}
776				candidates = append(candidates, branch)
777			}
778		}
779		if len(candidates) == 0 {
780			return "", nil
781		}
782		recordBranches := strings.Join(candidates, ", ")
783		if i := len(dir) - len("-01234567"); i > 0 {
784			candidates = append(candidates, dir[:i])
785		}

def add_import(s):
    if IMPORT in s:
        return s

    m = re.search(r'(?m)^import \(\n', s)

    # place before the first entire-brain import line, falling back to after "import (".
    lines = s.split('\n')
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if 'github.com/entireio/entire-brain/' in line and line.strip().startswith('"'):
            lines.insert(i, '\t' + IMPORT)
            return '\n'.join(lines)
    idx = s.index('import (\n') + len('import (\n')
    return s[:idx] + '\t' + IMPORT + '\n' + s[idx:]

generic = {

}

def apply(name, extra=None, deps_collect=False):
    p = root / name

# Git

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.
